stem:
A U-shaped tube contains some liquid. The liquid column in each half of the tube has length *L*, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

[[fig:f1]]

[[fig:f2]]

The liquid columns are displaced vertically. The liquid then oscillates in the tube. The liquid levels are displaced from the equilibrium positions as shown in Fig. 3.2.

The acceleration *a* of the liquid in the tube is related to the displacement *x* by the expression

*a* = −($\frac{g}{L}$)*x*

where *g* is the acceleration of free fall.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how the expression shows that the liquid in the tube is undergoing simple harmonic motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The length *L* of each liquid column is 18 cm.

Determine the period *T* of the oscillations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The oscillations of the liquid in the tube are damped.
In any one complete cycle of the oscillations, the amplitude decreases by 6.0% of its value at the beginning of the oscillation.

Determine the ratio

$\frac{\text{energy of oscillations after 3 cycles}}{\text{initial energy of oscillations}}$.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A U-shaped tube with equal liquid columns of length L in its two vertical arms, with dashed lines and arrows marking the equilibrium level and dimensions.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.2
figures.alt: A U-shaped tube showing the liquid displaced from its equilibrium level, with the displacement x marked at both arms.
